title.narrative: Integrated Humanitarian Assistance Program to Strengthen Critical Services in Conflict-Affected Populations (Syria)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to enhance access to life-saving and life-sustaining health services, with a particular emphasis on sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, for vulnerable populations, including internally displaced persons (IDPs). By focusing on underserved areas identified within the Standard Allocation Strategy of the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) in 2024, UNFPA seeks to deliver crucial SRH and nutrition services to pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Key initiatives will involve the rehabilitation of Primary Health Care (PHC) centers managed by the Directorate of Health (DOH) in Rural Damascus, which have suffered damage due to ongoing crises. The project will also encompass the replacement of essential medical equipment and furniture to ensure the availability of vital SRH services. Collaboration with UNOPS, a specialized UN agency, will facilitate resource mobilization to supply necessary medicines and aid. Furthermore, the project aims to promote the wellbeing of vulnerable groups, including adolescents, youth, and reproductive-age women, by integrating nutrition support for PLW and conducting disseminative activities focused on maternal nutrition, anemia, and infant care across 19 designated locations in various Syrian governorates. This holistic approach underscores a commitment to strengthening health system capacity, promoting community resilience, and ensuring continuity of care in a dynamic and challenging context.ltbrgtIn response to the increased cases of malnutrition identified in the 2023 SMART survey, UNFPA, in collaboration with its partners, will provide essential prevention nutrition supplements (LNS-PBWG) specifically designed for pregnant and lactating women (PLW) in targeted locations. Concurrently, UNFPA will bolster the health system's capacity by updating the national nutrition guidelines for PLW and enhancing the performance of healthcare providers in Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF). These initiatives aim to significantly reduce the incidence of malnutrition within the affected populations.ltbrgtOn the other hand, through this project, UNFPA in partnership with its implementing partners will ensure the provision of GBV life-saving services integrated with psychosocial support following the GBV minimum standard to reach the most vulnerable population groups in the targeted locations in three governorates: Rural Damascus, Dar'a and Deir-ez-Zor. GBV services will be provided by supporting the already existing Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) and the Integrated Mobile Teams (IMTs), the support will include 3 WGSS and 3 IMTs that run by UNFPA national NGOs IPs: Syrian Family Planning Association, Syrian Society for Social Development and Amelioration of Sanitary and Social Level Society. UNFPA provides full support to WGSS and IMTs operation by supporting the staff salaries, running costs, supplies and other related costs to ensure high quality of services in place. This project will ensure GBV case management services, multisector referrals for GBV survivors, risk mitigation and prevention services and activities for women and girls at risk. Female Dignity will be available through service provision to address the immediate needs and to reduce vulnerability and increase mobility of most at need. The support to new initiative which is the Young Mothers Club in 2 locations in Rural Damascus governorate to address the critical Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) information and services through intensive capacity building and empowerment intervention for the adolescent mothers. This project is planned to be implemented in 12 months period and the target/activities has been set accordingly and by taking into consideration the situation in the field and other administrative issueslt/pgt
